subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A researcher is studying the cells that bridge the innate and adaptive immune systems by capturing antigen in peripheral tissues and carrying it to lymph nodes to stimulate naive T cells. He wants to identify the cell type responsible for this link.
question: Which of the following cell types best serves as the link between the innate and adaptive immune systems through T-cell stimulation?
explanation_correct: Dendritic cells are highly phagocytic antigen-presenting cells that link the innate and adaptive immune systems. They capture antigen in peripheral tissues, migrate to lymphoid organs, and present processed antigen to naive T cells to initiate adaptive responses. They are the most potent activators of naive T cells. This positions them as the critical bridge between the two arms of immunity.

explanation_incorrect.A: Neutrophils are phagocytic innate cells of acute inflammation but do not serve as the principal link that stimulates naive T cells.
explanation_incorrect.B: Erythrocytes carry oxygen and carbon dioxide and play no role in antigen presentation or T-cell stimulation.
explanation_incorrect.C: Mast cells mediate allergic reactions and type I hypersensitivity but are not the APC that links innate and adaptive immunity via naive T-cell activation.
explanation_incorrect.E: Platelets are involved in primary hemostasis and are not antigen-presenting cells.

educationalObjective: Dendritic cells are highly phagocytic APCs that link innate and adaptive immunity by stimulating naive T cells.

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: An immunology laboratory analyzes the surface phenotype of a highly phagocytic antigen-presenting cell isolated from skin and lymphoid tissue. The cells are found to express both MHC class II molecules and receptors for the Fc portion of antibodies.
question: Which of the following best describes the surface molecules expressed by this cell type?

options.text: MHC class II and Fc receptors
MHC class I only, with no Fc receptors

explanation_correct: Dendritic cells are professional antigen-presenting cells that express MHC class II molecules and Fc receptors on their surface. MHC II allows them to present exogenous antigen to CD4+ helper T cells, while Fc receptors bind the Fc region of antibody-opsonized particles to enhance phagocytosis. They are highly phagocytic and also express pattern recognition receptors. This phenotype is consistent with the cell described.

explanation_incorrect.B: Dendritic cells express MHC class II as well as MHC class I and do express Fc receptors, so limiting them to MHC I only is incorrect.
explanation_incorrect.C: CD3 and CD28 are T-cell surface molecules involved in the T-cell receptor complex and costimulation, not dendritic cell markers.
explanation_incorrect.D: Glycoprotein Ib and IIb/IIIa are platelet surface receptors for von Willebrand factor and fibrinogen, not antigen-presenting cell molecules.
explanation_incorrect.E: CD19 and CD20 are B-cell surface markers, not the phenotype of dendritic cells.

educationalObjective: Dendritic cells express MHC class II and Fc receptors, supporting antigen presentation and opsonized-particle uptake.

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A virology researcher observes that a certain antigen-presenting cell can present exogenous viral antigens on MHC class I molecules, thereby activating CD8+ cytotoxic T cells, a process known as cross-presentation. She wants to identify the cell type uniquely capable of this.
question: Which of the following cell types is capable of cross-presenting exogenous antigens on MHC class I?
explanation_correct: Dendritic cells are uniquely capable of cross-presentation, the process by which exogenous antigens are presented on MHC class I molecules to activate CD8+ cytotoxic T cells. This allows the immune system to respond to viruses and tumors that do not directly infect the antigen-presenting cell. Dendritic cells can also present antigen on MHC II to CD4+ helper T cells. This dual presentation capacity underlies their central role in initiating adaptive immunity.

explanation_incorrect.A: B cells present antigen on MHC II to helper T cells but are not the principal cross-presenting cell for MHC I activation of CD8+ T cells.
explanation_incorrect.B: Macrophages are antigen-presenting cells that mainly present on MHC II, and they are not the classic cross-presenting cell type.
explanation_incorrect.C: Neutrophils are innate phagocytes and are not professional antigen-presenting cells capable of cross-presentation.
explanation_incorrect.D: Erythrocytes are anucleate oxygen-carrying cells and have no antigen-presenting capability.

educationalObjective: Dendritic cells can cross-present exogenous antigens on MHC class I to activate CD8+ cytotoxic T cells.
